learner_profile: 12th-grade graduate from India, non-English-medium background, limited technical vocabulary, zero prior AI knowledge.
must_cover_concepts: Why it matters (hallucination, outdated knowledge, private company data)
How it works (the 4 steps: chunking, embedding, retrieval, generation)
Crucial distinction: RAG never retrains or changes model weights
Limitations of RAG (garbage in garbage out, retrieval misses, latency and cost)
analogy: The Open-Book Exam: An LLM is like a student who has memorized a lot of general knowledge, but RAG is like giving that student a textbook to look at during an exam so they can answer specific questions accurately.
everyday_examples: A student using a textbook to answer a specific question about Indian History that isn't in their memory.
A bank employee searching through a private company manual to answer a customer's specific query about a new loan policy.
outline: Section 4: How Does RAG Work? (4 Steps)
Section 5: Worked Step-by-Step Example (Question -> Retrieved Passage -> Answer)
Section 8: Recap and Quick Check (Exactly 3 questions)
